title: Kojima et al. 2024 (Dataset A) — An auditory brain-computer interface based on selective attention to multiple tone streams
description: This dataset contains 64-channel EEG and 2-channel EOG recordings from 11 healthy participants performing a 3-class auditory brain-computer interface task based on auditory stream segregation. Musical piano tones were presented to the right ear as three tone streams, and participants attended to one stream while counting target stimuli, which elicited P300 responses. Classification with Riemannian geometry achieved accuracies over 80% for five subjects and over 75% for nine subjects.
methods_description: EEG (64 channels) and EOG (2 channels) were recorded at 1000 Hz with BrainAmp amplifiers and Ag-AgCl electrodes, referenced to the right earlobe. Piano tones (150 ms, SOA 180 ms) were presented to the right ear in three streams with 90% standard and 10% deviant tones. Each session had two task blocks of three 5-minute runs. Analysis used bandpass filtering, artifact rejection, xDAWN spatial filtering, and Riemannian geometry classification with 10-fold cross validation.
